explain.say: The sides of the Great Pyramid of Giza line up with north, south, east and west to within a small fraction of a degree, more than four and a half thousand years ago. Setting out is putting a design onto the ground that precisely. Here is the order a site engineer follows.

explain.say: Every corner has design coordinates. From a control station S at one hundred, one hundred, corner A is at one hundred and six, one hundred and eight. That is six metres east and eight north: ten metres away on a bearing of thirty six degrees fifty two minutes. The total station turns to that bearing and the pole is moved until the distance reads ten.

explain.say: Now the check. Our building is twelve metres by nine. If it is truly square, both diagonals are fifteen metres, the old three four five triangle made three times bigger. Look at the diagonal on the board. If one diagonal is longer, which corner do you think is out?

explain.say: The corner on the long diagonal's end is pushed out! Digging would destroy the pegs, so engineers fix profile boards a metre or two outside the trench. Strings stretched between nails on the boards mark each wall line, and levels for floors and trenches are carried from a temporary benchmark.

explain.say: Setting out tolerances are often just a few millimetres, so good engineers check every point twice, from a different station. A mistake here is built in concrete! Great work! Challenge: a garage is eight metres by six. What should each diagonal measure?

faq.q: How do you set out a building?
faq.a: Establish control points, set out the corners by coordinates or by bearing and distance, check the diagonals, then fix profile boards outside the excavation with strings for wall lines and transfer levels from a benchmark.

faq.q: How do you check a building is square?
faq.a: Measure both diagonals of the rectangle. If they are equal, and the sides are the right lengths, the corners are right angles. A 12 by 9 metre building has 15 metre diagonals.
asks: How do you check that a building is square?

faq.a: Horizontal boards on pegs set a short distance outside the excavation at each corner. Nails or saw cuts on them hold strings that mark the wall and trench lines after the corner pegs are dug out.
asks: What are profile boards used for?

faq.a: A triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 units has a right angle, because 3 squared plus 4 squared equals 5 squared. Builders use multiples like 6-8-10 to set out square corners.

faq.q: How do you set out a point by bearing and distance?
faq.a: Work out the bearing and distance from a control station to the design coordinates, set the total station on that bearing and move the prism along the line until the distance is correct.

facts: The sides of the Great Pyramid of Giza are aligned to the cardinal directions to within a few minutes of arc.
A rectangle 12 m by 9 m has 15 m diagonals: three times the 3-4-5 triangle.
